meta.description: Machine-readable graph of the oxen::quic C++ API — classes, methods, callbacks, and usage flows — derived from header files and session-router usage patterns.

properties.description: The central networking object. Binds a UDP socket to a local address, manages all QUIC connections (inbound and outbound), owns the event loop reference and a JobQueue. Non-copyable, non-movable, always held in shared_ptr. Created exclusively via the static factory function Endpoint::endpoint().

constructors.signature: static std::shared_ptr<Endpoint> endpoint(Loop& loop, const Address& local_addr, Opt&&... opts)
constructors.description: Factory function. Creates and returns a shared_ptr<Endpoint> bound to local_addr on the given Loop. Variadic opts configure ALPNs, callbacks, datagrams, static secrets, etc.

key_methods.description: Begin accepting inbound connections. Requires exactly one shared_ptr<TLSCreds>. Can only be called once. Additional opts set stream/connection callbacks and idle timeouts.

Initiate an outbound QUIC connection to `remote`. Returns a shared_ptr<Connection> immediately (connection handshake proceeds asynchronously). Opts can include TLSCreds, keep_alive, idle_timeout, outbound_alpns, and per-connection callbacks.

key_methods.signature: void close_connection(Connection& conn, io_error ec = {0}, std::optional<std::string> msg = std::nullopt)
key_methods.description: Close a specific connection, optionally sending an error code and message to the remote.
Close all connections, optionally filtered by direction (INBOUND or OUTBOUND).
Query all active connections, optionally filtered by direction.
Retrieve a connection by its internal reference ID.
Returns the local address this endpoint is bound to.
Inject a packet into the endpoint for manual routing mode (bypasses UDP socket).

callbacks.fires_when: A connection's handshake completes (both inbound and outbound). Passed as an opt to the factory function.
A connection closes or times out. ec is the error code. Passed as an opt to the factory function.
A datagram is received on any connection with datagrams enabled. Passed as an opt to the factory function.

endpoint_options: opt::enable_datagrams — enable datagram support, optionally with packet splitting
opt::outbound_alpns — default ALPNs for outbound connections
opt::inbound_alpns — accepted ALPNs for inbound connections
opt::alpns — sets both inbound and outbound simultaneously
opt::static_secret — deterministic secret for stateless reset tokens
opt::manual_routing — bypass UDP socket, use manual packet injection

properties.description: Represents a single QUIC session between two endpoints. Non-copyable, non-movable, always held in shared_ptr. Created internally by Endpoint (via connect() or incoming accept). Manages streams, datagrams, TLS session, and the ngtcp2 connection state.

key_methods.description: Open a new outgoing stream of type StreamT (default: Stream). Returns immediately; stream becomes ready when a stream ID is assigned by the QUIC layer.
Queue a typed stream object to receive the next incoming stream from the remote. Used by servers to pre-register a BTRequestStream before data arrives.
Returns the Datagrams pseudo-stream for this connection, or nullptr if datagrams are not enabled.
Initiate connection close, transmitting the error code to the remote.
Returns the remote's Ed25519 public key (empty if not yet known or not required).
Returns the negotiated ALPN string. Available after handshake completes.
Returns INBOUND or OUTBOUND.

key_methods.description: Direction helpers.
True if the TLS handshake has completed.

key_methods.signature: Address local() const / Address remote() const / Path path() const
key_methods.description: Access the local/remote addresses or full path of this connection.
Returns the unique internal reference ID assigned to this connection by the endpoint.
Returns the maximum datagram size negotiated for this connection (typically 1150-1450, or double with splitting).

Connection closes or times out. Can be set per-connection via IOContext opts.

properties.description: A Stream subclass implementing a reliable request/response protocol over a QUIC stream using bencoded (bt) framing. Supports named endpoint registration (like RPC methods), a generic fallback handler, request timeouts, and request IDs for matching responses. The primary control-plane transport in session-router.

constructors.signature: BTRequestStream(Connection& c, Endpoint& e, Opt&&... opts)
constructors.description: Protected constructor. Created via Connection::open_stream<BTRequestStream>(...) for outbound or Connection::queue_incoming_stream<BTRequestStream>(...) for inbound. Opts include stream_close_callback and generic_handler.

key_methods.signature: void command(std::string ep, std::span<const std::byte> body, Opt&&... opts)
key_methods.description: Send a request to the remote's named endpoint `ep` with the given body. Opts: std::function<void(message)> callback for the response, std::chrono::milliseconds timeout (default 10s). Without a callback, this is fire-and-forget.

key_methods.signature: void command(std::string ep, std::string_view body, Opt&&... opts)
key_methods.description: String_view overload of the above.
Register a named handler. When the remote sends a command to this endpoint name, the callback fires with the message.
Register a fallback handler for commands that don't match any named handler. Throw no_such_endpoint from it to send back a method-not-found error.

key_methods.signature: void respond(int64_t rid, std::span<const std::byte> body, bool error = false)
key_methods.description: Send a response to a previously received request identified by request ID.

callbacks.fires_when: A registered command is received from the remote (via register_handler), or when a response to a sent command arrives (via the callback passed to command()).

message_struct.description: The `message` struct received by handlers contains: type() — 'C' for command, 'R' for reply, 'E' for error; endpoint() — the endpoint name; body() — the payload; respond() — to send a reply; timed_out — true if this is a timeout notification; conn_rid() — the connection's reference ID.

properties.description: An IOChannel subclass representing the unreliable datagram channel on a QUIC connection. Supports optional packet splitting for payloads exceeding the single-datagram MTU (approximately doubling max size). Datagrams are unordered and unreliable but fast. Used for session data in session-router.

constructors.signature: Datagrams(Connection& c, Endpoint& e, dgram_data_callback data_cb = nullptr, size_t dgram_queue_limit = max)
constructors.description: Internal constructor. Not called directly — obtained via Connection::datagrams() after enabling datagrams on the Endpoint.

key_methods.signature: void send(std::span<const std::byte> data, std::shared_ptr<void> keep_alive = nullptr)
key_methods.description: Inherited from IOChannel. Queue a datagram for sending. Data must fit within get_max_datagram_size() (or double with splitting).
Convenience overload that moves data into a shared_ptr for keep-alive.

callbacks.fires_when: A datagram is received. The datagram struct contains: conn (Connection&), datagrams (Datagrams&), data (span of bytes). Can be set at Endpoint level or per-connection via IOContext.

splitting.description: When Splitting::ACTIVE is enabled on the Endpoint, datagrams larger than the single MTU are split into two pieces with 2-byte ID headers, reassembled transparently on the receiving end using a rotating buffer. This approximately doubles the max datagram payload.
modes: Splitting::NONE — no splitting, single MTU limit
Splitting::ACTIVE — split large datagrams into two pieces

properties.description: A libevent-based event loop running on its own thread. Owns the event_base and a main JobQueue. All Endpoint and Connection operations are dispatched through the Loop. Must outlive all Endpoints created on it. Non-copyable, non-movable.

constructors.description: Creates a new event loop and starts its thread.

key_methods.description: Execute f on the loop thread. If already on the loop thread, calls immediately; otherwise queues.
Execute f on the loop thread and block until the result is available. Returns the result.
Always queues f for later execution on the loop thread (never calls immediately).
Schedule a one-shot callback after a delay.

key_methods.signature: std::shared_ptr<Ticker> call_every(std::chrono::microseconds interval, Callable&& f, bool start_immediately = true)
key_methods.description: Schedule a repeating callback at the given interval. Returns a Ticker that can be started/stopped.
Create an idempotent event that can be manually triggered. Multiple wakes before execution = single call.

key_methods.signature: template<typename T, typename... Args> std::shared_ptr<T> make_shared(Args&&... args)
key_methods.description: Create a shared_ptr with a custom deleter that dispatches destruction to the loop thread.
Returns true if the caller is on the loop thread.

properties.description: TLS credential management for QUIC connections using GnuTLS with Ed25519 raw public keys. Supports authenticated (Ed25519 key pair) and unauthenticated (no client cert) modes. Provides 0-RTT session resumption (both inbound/server and outbound/client sides), client key verification, and session ticketing.

constructors.signature: static std::shared_ptr<GNUTLSCreds> make_from_ed_keys(std::string_view seed, std::string_view pubkey)
constructors.description: Create credentials from Ed25519 seed (32 bytes) and pubkey (32 bytes).
Create credentials from a combined Ed25519 seed+pubkey (64 bytes, libsodium format).
Create a no-credentials object for outbound connections that don't need client authentication.

key_methods.signature: void enable_inbound_0rtt(std::chrono::milliseconds anti_replay_window = 0s, std::chrono::seconds ticket_validity = 0s, size_t max_early_data = 0, anti_replay_add_cb = nullptr, std::span<const unsigned char> master_key = {})
key_methods.description: Enable server-side 0-RTT session resumption. Configures anti-replay, ticket validity, and optional master key for multi-instance deployments.
Enable client-side 0-RTT. store is called when a session ticket is received; extract is called when connecting to retrieve a stored ticket.
Enable client-side 0-RTT with built-in in-memory ticket storage.
Require incoming connections to provide an Ed25519 certificate. The callback verifies the key and returns true to accept, false to reject.
Request (but don't require) client keys. Callback receives empty key if client provides none.
Don't request or require client certificates (default).

callbacks.signature: std::function<bool(std::span<const unsigned char> key, std::string_view alpn)>
callbacks.fires_when: An incoming connection presents (or fails to present) a client certificate. Return true to accept, false to reject.

callbacks.signature: std::function<void(RemoteAddress remote, std::vector<unsigned char> data, std::chrono::sys_seconds expiry)>
callbacks.fires_when: A 0-RTT session ticket is received from a server (client-side).
A 0-RTT connection is being initiated and needs a stored session ticket (client-side).

properties.description: Internal struct that bundles per-connection configuration: TLS credentials, stream/datagram callbacks, and user_config (max_streams, keep_alive, idle_timeout, handshake_timeout, datagram settings, ALPNs). Created implicitly when you pass opts to listen() or connect(). The opts are parsed via variadic template handle_ioctx_opt overloads.

properties.description: A thread-safe task dispatch queue running on a Loop's event thread. Provides call(), call_get(), call_soon(), call_later(), and make_shared() with loop-thread destruction. Each Endpoint owns a JobQueue. Components with shorter lifetimes can create independent JobQueues to cancel pending jobs on destruction without affecting the Loop.

constructors.description: Creates a new job queue on the given Loop.

key_methods.description: Execute f on the loop thread. If already on the loop thread, calls immediately.
Execute f on the loop thread and block until the return value is available.
Always queues f for deferred execution on the loop thread.
Schedule execution after a delay.

key_methods.description: Create a shared_ptr with a custom deleter that dispatches destruction to this job queue.
Cancel all pending jobs and remove the queue's event. Terminal — cannot be restarted.
Returns true if the caller is on the loop thread.

properties.description: Base class for QUIC bidirectional streams. Supports send(), send_chunks(), pause()/resume(), watermarks for backpressure, FIN signaling. BTRequestStream inherits from this. Created via Connection::open_stream() or Connection::queue_incoming_stream().

key_methods.signature: void send(std::span<const std::byte> data, std::shared_ptr<void> keep_alive = nullptr)
key_methods.description: Queue data for sending on this stream.

key_methods.signature: void send_chunks(NextChunk next_chunk, done_callback, int simultaneous = 2)
key_methods.description: Stream large data in chunks. next_chunk is called repeatedly to get the next chunk; done is called when all chunks are queued.
Send a FIN bit to signal no more data will be sent.
Close the stream.
Flow control: pause stops extending the max stream data offset to the remote, resume unblocks.
Returns the QUIC stream ID, or negative if not yet assigned.
True if the stream has an assigned stream ID and can send data.

properties.description: How to set up a listening endpoint that accepts inbound QUIC connections.
sequence: 1. Create a Loop: auto loop = std::make_unique<quic::Loop>();
2. Create TLS credentials: auto creds = quic::GNUTLSCreds::make_from_ed_keys(seed, pubkey);
3. Configure client key verification: creds->request_client_keys(verify_callback); or creds->require_client_keys(verify_callback);
4. Optionally enable 0-RTT: creds->enable_inbound_0rtt(...);

5. Create endpoint via factory: auto ep = quic::Endpoint::endpoint(*loop, listen_addr, opt::static_secret{...}, on_conn_established_cb, on_conn_closed_cb, dgram_data_cb, opt::inbound_alpns{{...}}, opt::outbound_alpns{{...}}, opt::enable_datagrams{Splitting::ACTIVE});
6. Start listening: ep->listen(creds, quic::opt::idle_timeout{...});
7. In on_conn_established callback: set up streams (queue_incoming_stream<BTRequestStream>(...)).

properties.description: How to initiate an outbound QUIC connection to a remote peer.
sequence: 1. Have an existing Endpoint (from flow_listen or just a client endpoint).
2. Create a RemoteAddress: quic::RemoteAddress remote{remote_pubkey_view, remote_addr};
3. Call connect with per-connection opts: auto conn = ep->connect(remote, tls_creds, quic::opt::keep_alive{10s}, quic::opt::idle_timeout{33s});
4. The connect() returns immediately with a shared_ptr<Connection>.
5. Open a control stream: auto ctrl = conn->open_stream<quic::BTRequestStream>(close_cb, quic::opt::stream_notify);
6. Register handlers and/or send commands on the stream.
7. The on_conn_established callback fires when handshake completes.

properties.description: How to send a request on a BTRequestStream and handle the response.
sequence: 1. Obtain a BTRequestStream (from open_stream or queue_incoming_stream).
2. Send a command: stream->command("endpoint_name", body_bytes, [](quic::message m) { /* response handler */ }, std::chrono::milliseconds{5000});
3. The callback fires when the response arrives or the request times out.
4. In the callback: check m.timed_out, m.is_error(), then use m.body() for the response payload.
5. For fire-and-forget (no response expected): stream->command("endpoint_name", body_bytes); — omit the callback.

properties.description: How to register handlers for incoming BTRequestStream commands.
sequence: 1. Obtain a BTRequestStream.
2. Register named handlers: stream->register_handler("ping", [](quic::message m) { m.respond("pong"); });
3. Register multiple handlers for different endpoints: stream->register_handler("fetch_rcs", handler_fn);
4. Optionally register a generic fallback: stream->register_generic_handler([](quic::message m) { /* handle or throw no_such_endpoint */ });
5. When a command arrives matching a registered name, the corresponding callback fires with a message object.
6. Call m.respond(body) or m.respond(body, true) for error responses.

properties.description: How to send an unreliable datagram on a connection.
sequence: 1. Endpoint must have been created with opt::enable_datagrams (optionally with Splitting::ACTIVE).
2. After connection is established, get the Datagrams channel: auto dg = conn->datagrams();
3. Check that datagrams are enabled: if (!dg) return; // not enabled
4. Send data: dg->send(std::move(data_vector));
5. Data must fit within conn->get_max_datagram_size() (or double with splitting).

properties.description: How to receive incoming datagrams.
sequence: 1. Pass a dgram_data_callback when creating the Endpoint (endpoint-level) or in the IOContext opts (per-connection).
2. The callback signature: [](quic::datagram dgram) { ... }
3. Inside the callback: dgram.data is a span<const std::byte> of the received datagram.
4. dgram.conn is a reference to the Connection it arrived on.
5. To take ownership: auto owned = std::move(dgram).extract(); — returns a vector<byte>.
6. For split datagrams, reassembly is automatic and transparent.

properties.description: How to configure GnuTLS credentials for authenticated QUIC connections.
sequence: 1. For service nodes (relay-to-relay): auto creds = quic::GNUTLSCreds::make_from_ed_keys(seed_32bytes, pubkey_32bytes);
2. For clients (no cert required): auto creds = quic::GNUTLSCreds::make_unauthenticated();
3. For servers accepting relays: creds->request_client_keys([](span<const uint8_t> key, string_view alpn) -> bool { /* verify key against ALPN */ });
4. Enable server-side 0-RTT: creds->enable_inbound_0rtt(0s, 48h);
5. Enable client-side 0-RTT with custom storage: creds->enable_outbound_0rtt(store_cb, extract_cb);
6. Pass creds to listen() and/or connect() as an opt.

properties.description: Documents how session-router uses the libquic API — the specific ALPN strings, callback patterns, and configuration options extracted from the session-router source code.

alpn_strings.BOOTSTRAP_ALPN: Session_Router_BS — bootstrap connections (short-lived, single bfetch_rcs command)

endpoint_configuration.description: Single Endpoint per node, created in srouter::link::Endpoint constructor.
endpoint_configuration.static_secret: Derived from Ed25519 secret key via blake2b with domain separator 'Session Router static shared secret key'
endpoint_configuration.outbound_alpns: RELAY_ALPN for service nodes, CLIENT_ALPN for clients
endpoint_configuration.inbound_alpns: [RELAY_ALPN, CLIENT_ALPN, BOOTSTRAP_ALPN] for service nodes only
endpoint_configuration.tls_creds: make_from_ed_keys for service nodes, make_unauthenticated for clients
endpoint_configuration.0rtt_inbound: Enabled for service nodes with 0s replay window, 48h ticket validity
endpoint_configuration.0rtt_outbound: Enabled with custom store/extract callbacks backed by NodeDB
endpoint_configuration.client_keys: request_client_keys (not require) — relays must provide valid Ed25519 key matching RELAY_ALPN; clients may omit

relay_inbound.idle_timeout: 63s (RELAY_INBOUND_IDLE_TIMEOUT = max of client and relay timeouts)
relay_inbound.description: Server-side idle timeout set to accommodate both relay and client peers.

bootstrap.description: Short-lived connection for bootstrap RC fetching.

stream_patterns.outbound_control_stream: conn->open_stream<quic::BTRequestStream>(close_cb, quic::opt::stream_notify) — opens stream ID 0 with immediate notify
stream_patterns.inbound_control_stream: conn->queue_incoming_stream<quic::BTRequestStream>(close_cb) — pre-registers a BTRequestStream for the expected incoming stream
registered_commands: path_build — relay-only: construct a path hop
bfetch_rcs — bootstrap-only: fetch bootstrap relay contacts

datagram_patterns.receive: Endpoint-level dgram_data_callback transfers handling to router loop via router._jq->call()

connection_wrapper.description: srouter::link::Connection bundles: shared_ptr<quic::Connection> conn, shared_ptr<quic::Datagrams> datagrams (from conn->datagrams()), shared_ptr<quic::BTRequestStream> control_stream

redundancy_handling.description: Relay pairs can have bidirectional connections. The 'winner' is determined by comparing RouterIDs. After REDUNDANT_LINGER (20s), the 'loser' connection is closed. This prevents message loss during the race to establish connections.

properties.description: Endpoint runs on a Loop's event thread. The Loop must outlive the Endpoint.
Endpoint::connect() creates outbound Connections; incoming connections are accepted and created internally.
Each Endpoint owns a JobQueue (public member: job_queue) for dispatching work to the loop thread.
TLSCreds are passed to listen() and connect() for TLS handshake configuration.
Connection::open_stream<BTRequestStream>() and queue_incoming_stream<BTRequestStream>() create BTRequestStream instances.
Connection owns a Datagrams instance (accessible via datagrams()) when datagrams are enabled.
Connection::open_stream() and queue_incoming_stream() create Stream (or subclass) instances.
Connection holds a reference to its owning Endpoint for packet sending and CID management.
Outbound connections are created with a RemoteAddress specifying the target's pubkey and address.
BTRequestStream inherits from Stream, adding bencoded request/response framing.
JobQueue dispatches tasks onto the Loop's event thread.
Loop owns a main_queue JobQueue.
RemoteAddress inherits from Address, adding a remote public key.
0-RTT store/extract callbacks receive RemoteAddress to identify the remote peer.

properties.step: 4-5. Use returned Connection to open streams

properties.description: Session-router creates a single Endpoint per node with full configuration.
Session-router configures GNUTLSCreds with Ed25519 keys, 0-RTT, and client key verification.
Session-router uses BTRequestStream as the primary control-plane protocol with 10+ registered commands.
Session-router uses datagrams with active splitting for session data messages.
